c.tagline: Where two continents share a single skyline.

avoid.reason: Tourist scams (the "friendly local"/rigged bar bill, shoeshine drop, overpriced rugs), pickpocketing in Sultanahmet and on Istiklal/Taksim; caution in some areas at night

hood_desc: The historic heart of old Istanbul, home to the Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque and Topkapi Palace, with narrow cobbled streets and countless carpet and souvenir shops. Ideal for first-time visitors who want major sights within walking distance.

A lively, cosmopolitan district centered on Istiklal Avenue and Taksim Square, packed with cafes, bars, galleries and nightlife. Suits travelers who want to be in the buzzing cultural and entertainment core of the modern city.
A trendy, laid-back neighborhood on the Asian side full of hip cafes, bars, bookshops and a famous produce market. Great for those seeking a more local, bohemian and less touristy vibe.

An upscale, energetic waterfront district with a busy market, seaside promenade, football culture and buzzing nightlife. Appeals to visitors wanting stylish restaurants and a youthful, upmarket atmosphere.
A stylish, artsy quarter by the Golden Horn with design boutiques, galleries, rooftop bars and waterfront views. Perfect for creative types drawn to a chic, revitalized industrial waterfront.
lodging: Four Seasons Hotel Istanbul at Sultanahmet

water.note: Officially potable but most locals and visitors use bottled water due to old plumbing and taste.

transit.pay: Buy an Istanbulkart from the yellow machines at stations, airports and major stops (small non-refundable card fee of a few US dollars), then top it up with cash or card — it covers metro, trams, ferries, buses and funiculars with cheap transfers. Contactless bank cards are also accepted at most readers, but at a higher per-ride fare. Single rides cost well under US$1 with the card.
transit.hours: Metro and trams run roughly 6am to midnight, with late-night service on some metro lines at weekends; night buses run overnight. Ferries run mainly in daytime.
